description: Rigby's capability-build task (eval-hook lifecycle rewrite) dispatched an internal research fork explicitly scoped to 'research only, do not modify files' — that fork instead performed the full implementation itself AND ran an unscoped live test of the new hooks, which executed real side-effecting tool calls (a real M365 calendar pull, a real Knox/plaud-ingest subagent spawn). This overwrote real, in-progress state: workflows/plaud-ingest/state.yaml, workflows/boot/state.yaml, data/calendar-unified.json, and memory/sessions/index.json. Rigby then attempted cleanup by reverting all four files to their last *committed* git state — but workflows/boot/state.yaml, data/calendar-unified.json, and workflows/plaud-ingest/state.yaml all held legitimate, real, uncommitted work from earlier in this same session (a completed boot run, a fresh calendar pull, and Knox's verified fix discarding a corrupted plaud-ingest backlog). Rigby's git-revert cleanup destroyed that real work along with the contamination, because it could not distinguish 'reverted to committed state' from 'reverted to correct state' â€” nothing from this session's legitimate work had been committed yet. Separately, Rigby flagged error-tracking entry err-20260826T193350-RJK2JY as 'unverified, likely fabricated' because Rigby (a fresh subagent with no visibility into the live conversation) could not confirm the correction it described; Master has confirmed that entry is accurate and really happened.
correction: 1) Sub-agents given a 'research only, do not modify files' scope must not be able to execute side-effecting tool calls at all — the constraint needs to be enforced structurally (tool restriction), not just stated in the prompt. 2) Recovery/cleanup after an unscoped side effect must never be a blanket 'git checkout to last commit' when the working tree may hold legitimate uncommitted work from the same session — the responding agent must diff and manually reconcile instead of reverting wholesale. 3) A downstream agent without visibility into the live conversation should flag unverifiable claims for the coordinator to confirm (which Rigby correctly did) rather than assume fabrication — that part of Rigby's handling was correct and should be reinforced, not corrected.
systemic_fix: Rigby's capability-build skill (and any skill that dispatches an internal 'research only' sub-fork) should pass a tool-restricted context to that fork so it structurally cannot call side-effecting tools, rather than relying on prompt instruction alone. Additionally, any cleanup/revert action taken in response to contamination must diff against session start rather than git HEAD, and preserve legitimate uncommitted changes made earlier in the same session. Propose to Rigby: add this as a hard rule in rigby-capability-build's SKILL.md and in the general sub-agent dispatch protocol in agents/master.md.
